newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders pinned at highs in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders pinned at highs in thin trade.

text.p: Overnight guilders remained pinned to the previous day's highs on Thursday in thin trade ahead of the announcement of a new short-term liquidity pact.
Call rates were unchanged at 3.18/31 percent bid/offer, quoting higher than one to three-month guilders, which were priced at 3.18/26 percent bid/offer.
"The new money market instruments means banks have to be much more precise about their liquidity needs, so most are playing it safe," one dealer said.
Under the new regime, effective since last Friday, players may no longer hold a negative balance with the central bank.
Instead, accounts are brought into balance at the end of the day with a credit obtained from the central bank at the new marginal advance rate, currently pegged at 4.5 percent.
This compares with a rate on special advances of 2.9 percent, traditionally the marker for call rates under the old system.
Dealers said call rates would likely remain at current high levels until the market accustomed itself to working with the new instruments and fine-tuning their money needs.
The guilder was fixed at 112.525 guilders per 100 marks, down from Wednesday when it traded at around 112.49.
